text: {"overall_winner": "A", "qualities": [{"evidence": "Essay A directly quotes the article with page citations, e.g., \"If the technology fails and someone is injured, who is at fault the driver or the manufacturer?\" (Driverless Cars,9).", "quality": "Use of textual evidence", "description": "The essay grounds its claims in specific quoted details from the source article, whereas Essay B only loosely paraphrases one anecdote without citing it."}, {"evidence": "Essay A organizes points around distinct reasons: hacking/sensor failure, legal liability, and testing restrictions, each developed in its own paragraph.", "quality": "Structured argumentation", "description": "The essay presents multiple clearly separated supporting reasons that build a coherent case, while Essay B drifts between a general endorsement and an unrelated concern about price."}, {"evidence": "Essay A maintains a consistent position against driverless cars throughout, tying each paragraph back to safety and reliability concerns.", "quality": "Focused thesis development", "description": "Every body paragraph advances the stated position with relevant support, whereas Essay B's argument loses focus and never returns to defend its claim with evidence."}, {"evidence": "Essay A engages with the article's discussion of legal liability and state laws, addressing the counterpoint that some states allow semi-autonomous testing.", "quality": "Acknowledgment of complexity", "description": "The essay engages with the nuances and complications of the issue rather than treating it as a simple matter of preference."}, {"evidence": "Essay A includes a conclusion that synthesizes its main points about unpredictability, laws, and safety.", "quality": "Effective conclusion", "description": "The essay closes by restating and reinforcing its argument, while Essay B ends abruptly with a vague hope to see the vehicle in action."}]}
